title: Quietest time to visit Rome
author: Matt
intro: The quietest time to visit Rome is January and February, outside New Year, with November close behind. Here's when the crowds are lightest, what the weather is like, and the days of the week to avoid at the big sights.
seo_title: Quietest time to visit Rome: January to February
seo_description: January and February are Rome's quietest months, with November close behind. Avoid Easter, Saturdays and the Vatican's free Sunday. Month by month.

sections.heading: The short answer
sections.text:
- **Quietest:** January and February
- **Quiet and milder:** November
- **Busiest:** Easter to October
- **Worst day at the Vatican:** the free Sunday

Rome is never empty, and the big sights have queues all year. But in winter you'll share the Sistine Chapel and the Colosseum with far fewer people, and hotels are at their cheapest. The trade-off is shorter days and cooler, sometimes wet weather.

sections.heading: Rome month by month
sections.text:
| Months | Crowds | Typical high | Good to know |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| January to February | Lowest | 12-13°C | Cheapest hotels, except New Year |
| March | Rising | 16°C | Busy around Easter, which is 28 March in 2027 |
| April to June | High | 19-28°C | Peak season for groups and city breaks |
| July to August | High | 31°C | Very hot; many locals leave in August |
| September to October | High | 22-27°C | Popular for the warm, settled weather |
| November | Low | 17°C | Quiet, but the wettest month |
| December | Mixed | 13°C | Quiet early on, busy at Christmas |

The temperatures are average daytime highs from our [Rome guide](/destinations/rome).

sections.heading: January and February: the quietest months
sections.text:
Once the Christmas and New Year visitors go home, after Epiphany on 6 January, Rome has its quietest weeks of the year. Hotels drop their prices, and at the Vatican Museums or the Borghese Gallery you'll often have room to stand and look.

It's cool rather than cold, at about 12 to 13°C by day, with plenty of bright, clear days between the rain. Evenings are chilly, and the sun sets at about 5pm in January, so plan the outdoor sights, like the Forum and the Palatine, for the middle of the day and save museums for later.

Local knowledge: Rome's winter sales usually start in early January and run for several weeks, so it's a good time for shopping on Via del Corso and around the Spanish Steps.

sections.heading: November: quiet and milder
sections.text:
November is almost as quiet as January, but warmer, at about 17°C. It's the wettest month, though, so expect some showery days and pack an umbrella. The upside is that autumn food is at its best, with new-season olive oil, artichokes and chestnuts.

Early December is quiet too, before Christmas. The city fills up around 8 December, a public holiday, and stays busy through the Christmas markets and New Year.

sections.heading: Days and times to avoid
sections.text:
Even in a quiet month, a few days are much busier than the rest:

- **The last Sunday of the month:** entry to the Vatican Museums is free, and the queues are the longest of the month. The museums are otherwise closed on Sundays.
- **Wednesday mornings at St Peter's:** the Pope's general audience is usually held then, so the basilica can be closed or busy.
- **The first Sunday of the month:** many state museums and sites, including the Colosseum, are often free, which brings big crowds.
- **Saturdays:** the busiest day for day-trippers and weekend breaks.
- **Easter and Christmas:** the busiest weeks of the year in Rome.

Watch out: the Trevi Fountain has charged a €2 fee to visit the basin area since February 2026, with timed entry during the day. It's still free to see from the square, and early in the morning or late at night it's much quieter.

sections.heading: How to beat the crowds in any month
sections.text:
If you can only go in spring or summer, you can still dodge the worst of it:

- **Book timed tickets** for the Colosseum, the Vatican Museums and the Borghese Gallery, which needs a booking in any case.
- **Start early:** the first entry slot is the calmest at almost every sight.
- **Visit St Peter's at opening time**, before the tour groups arrive.
- **Stay overnight in the centre**, so you can walk the old streets in the evening when the day-trippers have gone.

Or pair Rome with somewhere calmer. [Naples](/destinations/naples) is about an hour away by fast train, and [Florence](/destinations/florence) is about an hour and a half. Our [quietest time to visit Venice](/blog/quietest-time-to-visit-venice) post covers Italy's other crowded city.

sections.heading: Planning your trip
sections.text:
Rome is about 2½ hours from most UK airports, with direct flights all year to Fiumicino and Ciampino. It's an hour ahead of the UK. The [holidays in Italy](/destinations/holidays-in-italy) page has more ideas, and our [city breaks](/destinations/city-breaks) page compares Rome with other short trips.

If you're torn between Rome and somewhere else for a winter break, add them all to somewhere.party and let the draw decide.

faqs.question: What is the least crowded month in Rome?
faqs.answer: January, once the New Year visitors have gone, followed by February. November is also quiet and a little warmer.

faqs.question: Is Rome worth visiting in winter?
faqs.answer: Yes. Days are about 12 to 13°C in January and February, the queues are much shorter and hotels are cheaper. The trade-offs are shorter days and some rain.

faqs.question: What day are the Vatican Museums least busy?
faqs.answer: Weekday afternoons in low season are usually calmest. Avoid Saturdays and the free last Sunday of the month.

faqs.question: Do you have to pay to see the Trevi Fountain?
faqs.answer: Since February 2026, visitors pay €2 to go down to the basin area during the day. You can still see it for free from the square.
